label: Bionda dell'Adamello

names.text: Bionda and Mustàscia are the breed's names given in the Wikipedia article, which also says it was formerly known as the Capra Bionda or Mustàscia.

about.text: The Bionda dell'Adamello is a goat breed from Val Camonica in Brescia province, Lombardy, northern Italy, named after the Adamello massif. Its milk goes mainly into Mascarpì, a kind of ricotta, and Fatulì, a smoked caprino cheese with PAT status. The herd book was activated in 1997.

sources.text: All from the Wikipedia article: region, Adamello name, Mascarpì as the main product, Fatulì with PAT status, herd book activated 1997.

origin.place: Val Camonica, Brescia province, Lombardy; mainly Val Saviore and the Brescia mountains, with some animals in Bergamo and Trento

sources.text: Wikipedia: region of origin and distribution. The article describes "ancient origin" and documents the breed before and after the Second World War. A c.1760 painting by Francesco Londonio shows a goat of this type, so the type existed by then; no formation date is given, so none is recorded.

Wikipedia: secondiparous nannies 303 ± 108 kg, pluriparous nannies 361 ± 122 kg per lactation. The min and max are those two means, not a spread. The recording place, year and lactation length are not given.
Wikipedia: averages 3.16% milk fat and 2.97% milk protein. Lactose and solids are not given.
Wikipedia: the milk is used mainly for cheese (Mascarpì and Fatulì).
Wikipedia: registered population at end of 2013 as reported by FAO's DAD-IS.
Wikipedia: registered population at end of 2013 as reported by the Associazione Nazionale della Pastorizia. The two sources disagree; both are kept.
Wikipedia: FAO (2007) listed the breed as not at risk. Not checked against the current DAD-IS record.

facts.v: A smoked caprino cheese made from the breed's milk, with PAT (traditional agri-food product) status, and listed in the Slow Food Ark of Taste.

sources.text: Wikipedia: Fatulì, PAT status, Ark of Taste (Slow Food Foundation).

facts.v: A kind of ricotta, and the main product made from the breed's milk.

sources.text: Wikipedia: Mascarpì described as a kind of ricotta and the main product. No protected status is given.

gaps: Searched for: a formation date (none in the sources); the current DAD-IS population and risk status (only 2007 and 2013 figures found, and no DAD-IS page was fetched); lactation length (not in Wikipedia); recording place and year of the yield figures (not given); lactose and solids (not given). Everything here comes from one Wikipedia article, so confidence is medium.
